kangaroo-ca-2015-g0910-06.title: Two equations
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0910-06.body:
Let $r$ be the number of right and $w$ the number of wrong answers. Then $r + w = 25$ and $2r - w = 5$. Adding: $3r = 30$, so $r = 10$ and $w = 15$.

**Answer: (C) 15**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0910-06.title: Start from all wrong
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0910-06.body:
If all 25 answers were wrong he would have $-25$ points. Turning one wrong answer into a right one changes the score by $+3$. To reach $5$ he needs $\frac{5 - (-25)}{3} = 10$ right answers, so $25 - 10 = 15$ wrong ones.

**Answer: (C) 15**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0910-10.title: Possible angle triples
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0910-10.body:
The three angles must add up to $180^\circ$ using only $40, 50, 90, 100$.
- With $100^\circ$: the other two add to $80^\circ$, so $40 + 40$.
- With $90^\circ$ (and no $100^\circ$): the other two add to $90^\circ$, so $40 + 50$.
- Without $90^\circ$ or $100^\circ$: the angles are from $\{40, 50\}$ and sum to at most $150^\circ$ — impossible.

So the shapes are $(100^\circ, 40^\circ, 40^\circ)$ and $(90^\circ, 50^\circ, 40^\circ)$. For each shape, the area fixes the size (scaling by $k$ multiplies the area by $k^2$), so there is exactly one triangle of area 1 of each shape: 2 triangles.

**Answer: (C) 2**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0910-13.title: Count the faces
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0910-13.body:
Each picture shows three faces that meet at a corner. The first picture shows YES, YES and maybe; the second shows no, no and YES — so the second picture shows the three faces we could not see in the first (it cannot show the maybe face or two of the YES faces again). Altogether the six faces are: YES three times, no twice and maybe once.

$$P(\text{YES}) = \frac36 = \frac12.$$

**Answer: (B) $\frac12$**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0910-16.title: Factorise 2015
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0910-16.body:
$2015 = 5 \cdot 13 \cdot 31$, so the factor pairs are $1 \cdot 2015$, $5 \cdot 403$, $13 \cdot 155$ and $31 \cdot 65$. Nobody is 155, 403 or 2015 years old, so the father is 65 and the son 31. The difference is $65 - 31 = 34$.

(Of the listed differences only 34 occurs at all: the four pairs have differences 2014, 398, 142 and 34.)

**Answer: (D) 34**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0910-17.title: Use the 'mixed' label
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0910-17.body:
Take one candy from the dispenser labelled "mixed". Its label is wrong, so it contains only one flavour — the flavour of the candy he got, say cherry. Now the dispenser labelled "lemon" is not lemon (wrong label) and not cherry (that one is found), so it is mixed. The last dispenser is lemon.

Zero candies cannot be enough: there are two ways to derange three labels, and without any information Robert cannot tell them apart. So the minimum is 1.

**Answer: (A) 1**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0910-20.title: Equilateral triangle
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0910-20.body:
$Q$ lies on the quarter-circles centred at $C$ and $D$ (radius 1), so $QC = QD = CD = 1$: triangle $QCD$ is equilateral and $\angle QDC = 60^\circ$. Hence $\angle ADQ = 90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ$.

Triangle $ADQ$ is isosceles with $DA = DQ = 1$, so $\angle DAQ = \angle DQA = \frac{180^\circ - 30^\circ}{2} = 75^\circ$, and $\angle QAB = 90^\circ - 75^\circ = 15^\circ$. By symmetry $\angle QBA = 15^\circ$ too, so
$$\angle AQB = 180^\circ - 15^\circ - 15^\circ = 150^\circ.$$

**Answer: (E) $150^\circ$**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0910-20.title: Coordinates
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0910-20.body:
Put $B = (0,0)$, $C = (1,0)$, $D = (1,1)$, $A = (0,1)$. The point at distance 1 from both $C$ and $D$ near side $AB$ is $Q = (1 - \frac{\sqrt3}{2}, \frac12)$. The half-angle at $Q$ in the isosceles triangle $AQB$ satisfies
$$\tan\tfrac{\angle AQB}{2} = \frac{1/2}{1 - \sqrt3/2} = \frac{1}{2 - \sqrt3} = 2 + \sqrt3 = \tan 75^\circ,$$
so $\angle AQB = 150^\circ$.

**Answer: (E) $150^\circ$**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0910-26.title: Express $a_7$ through $a_1, a_2$
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0910-26.body:
Let $a_1 = x$, $a_2 = y$. Then $a_3 = x + y$, $a_4 = x + 2y$, $a_5 = 2x + 3y$, $a_6 = 3x + 5y$, $a_7 = 5x + 8y$. The sequence is fixed by $x, y$, and all terms are positive integers exactly when $x, y$ are.

So we count positive integer solutions of $5x + 8y = 2015$. Since $5 \mid 2015$, $5 \mid 8y$, so $y = 5k$ and $x = 403 - 8k$. We need $k \ge 1$ and $403 - 8k \ge 1$, i.e. $k \le 50$. That gives 50 sequences.

**Answer: (D) 50**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0910-30.title: Complementary key sets
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0910-30.body:
Each director holds a 3-element subset of the 6 locks' keys. Two directors together can open the safe exactly when their two sets together contain all 6 keys, i.e. when one set is the **complement** of the other.

There are $\binom63 = 20$ possible key sets, and they split into $10$ complementary pairs. From each pair at most one set may be used, so there are at most 10 directors; choosing one set from every pair gives 10 directors, no two of which can open the safe.

**Answer: (C) 10**
